title: P42-P2-R4 — Demand-Indexed Repair Transition Systems: Source-Realized Option Fibers, Non-Congruence of Present Behavioral Quotients, Order-Sensitive Change Paths & Conditional Lifecycle Reversal
origin: Only source-grounded architecture structure interacting with future requirement stream qualifies; response distinguishability is auxiliary

SINGLE.description: original Echo with one verb route

SPLIT.description: same original Echo with same verb route plus generic fallback
SPLIT.old_contract: identical to SINGLE for the two D0 requests

source_edit_grammar.ADD_FALLBACK: SINGLE => SPLIT; exactly one added original-Echo route registration in authored Go source
source_edit_grammar.REMOVE_FALLBACK: SPLIT => SINGLE; delete exactly the same route registration
source_edit_grammar.proof_scope: only these two locally authored source assemblies, not all Go edits

cost_policy.late_action_count: number of add/remove source registration operations; 0 for no-op; not human-hours or full patch churn
cost_policy.cost_is_vector: keep initial source registrations, subsequent edit count, final source registrations and client-preservation separately; no single calibrated S/L/C/A/Q score
cost_policy.conditional_sensitivity_not_measured: for a one-shot legacy probability p, denial probability 1-p and hypothetical late edit weight w, cost_single=1+p*w, cost_split=2+(1-p)*w, split preferred iff (2p-1)*w>1; not estimated p or w
cost_policy.asymmetric_policy: if w=2, p>0.75 is a possible mathematical threshold, not empirical forecasting evidence

formal_claims: present D0 behavior equivalence DOES NOT determine minimum source edit count under future demand
opposite one-step demands produce opposite conditional late edit preference
source-edit action applicability cannot be reconstructed from frozen D0 observations alone
sequence order LN versus NL changes number of edits per initial architecture
historical source structure is not replaced by arbitrary synthetic alternate worlds
classic_rivals: finite labeled transition systems and demand games
classical source-aware guarded CSP/shortest-path dynamic programming
Parnas information hiding and real options
limits: new two-state authored source assemblies are real Go using unchanged upstream router, NOT historical maintainer design alternatives
source-state transitions are independently verified finite source patches, NOT a universal Go edit calculus
no novelty claim over standard graph shortest paths, dynamic programming or featured transition systems
historical upstream rights UNKNOWN; no writes to labstack/echo
no quantified real developer productivity or runtime performance
